BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to reporting identity theft cases; adding a newsection to chapter 43.43 RCW; and adding a new section to chapter 9.35RCW.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 43.43 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The Washington state patrol shall create and maintain a callcenter and a statewide web site that shall be available for the filingof incident reports relating to identity crimes under chapter 9.35 RCW. (2) The web site shall contain instructions to the general publicon how to utilize the web site to create and file an incident reportrelating to identity theft. At a minimum, when filing an incidentreport, the web site shall request, but is not limited to: The name ofthe person completing the form, the complainant's name, address, phonenumber, date and place that the incident may have occurred, adescription of the identity theft crime that has taken place, and anyother information that is deemed necessary according to the Washingtonstate patrol. p. 1 HB 2054 (3) The call center shall take all relevant information regardingthe complainant's identity theftrelated case for the creation of anincident report. At a minimum, when filing an incident report, thecall center shall request, but is not limited to: The name of theperson completing the form, the complainant's name, address, phonenumber, date and place that the incident may have occurred, adescription of the identity theft crime that has taken place, and anyother information that is deemed necessary according to the Washingtonstate patrol. The call center shall be open and available to thepublic Monday through Friday from eight a.m. until five p.m. (4) The Washington state patrol must provide the complainant witha response, a case number, and copy of any incident report filed byphone or via internet within forty eight hours.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 9.35 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) A person who has learned or reasonably suspects that his or herfinancial information or means of identification has been unlawfullyobtained, used by, or disclosed to another, as described in thischapter, may file an incident report with the Washington state patrolvia the call center or web site established in section 1 of this act.The Washington state patrol shall create a police incident report ofthe matter, provide the complainant with a copy of that report with acorresponding case number within fortyeight hours, and may refer theincident report to another appropriate law enforcement agency. (2) Nothing in this section shall be construed to require a lawenforcement agency to investigate reports claiming identity theft. Anincident report filed under this section is not required to be countedas an open case for purposes of compiling open case statistics. (3) Nothing in this section shall be construed to prohibit a personfrom filing an incident report with a law enforcement agency other thanthe Washington state patrol.
